title: Have political appointees sign OMB funding apportionments
proposal: OMB's political appointees (Program Associate Directors), not career staff, should personally review and sign the apportionments that release funds to agencies, restoring a Trump-era practice.
quote: No Director should be chosen who is unwilling to restore apportionment decision-making to the PADs’ personal review

title: Appoint an OMB General Counsel willing to challenge legal precedents
proposal: The OMB Director should appoint a General Counsel who is creative and willing to challenge legal precedents that protect the status quo.
quote: The Director must ensure the appointment of a General Counsel who is respected yet creative and fearless

title: Unify OMB under a strong Deputy Director ("One OMB")
proposal: The OMB Director should give a strong Deputy Director authority over OMB's management, budget, and regulatory offices so OMB speaks with one voice for the President.
quote: OMB should work toward a “One OMB” position on behalf of the President and represent that view during the various policymaking processes.

title: Set a fiscal goal early in the budget process
proposal: The OMB Director should give the President a goal for reducing federal fiscal problems early in budget planning, to guide the budget proposals that follow.
quote: The OMB Director should present a fiscal goal to the President early in the budget development process to address the federal government’s fiscal irresponsibility.

title: Split OMB budget offices and add political leaders
proposal: OMB's six Resource Management Offices should be broken into smaller subject areas, each with more political appointees (PADs) and a Deputy PAD, to give more political direction over agency policy.
quote: the existing six RMOs should be divided into smaller subject-matter areas, allowing for more PADs, and each of these PADs should have a Deputy PAD.

title: Bring back administrative PAYGO
proposal: The President should again require 'administrative pay-as-you-go,' meaning agencies' discretionary actions that raise spending must be offset so they are budget-neutral.
quote: the President should reintroduce the concept of administrative pay-as-you-go, or administrative PAYGO.

title: Use federal contracts to counter corporate 'woke' policies
proposal: OMB's procurement office should seek more transparency about who receives federal contracts and grants and use government contracting to push back against what the authors call woke corporate policies.
quote: obtaining transparency about entities that are awarded federal contracts and grants and by using government contracts to push back against woke policies in corporate America.
agency: OMB / Office of Federal Procurement Policy

title: Tie agency performance goals to the President's agenda
proposal: The OMB Director should have its performance office set yearly performance goals and review processes for agencies that reflect the President's agenda.
quote: The Director should instruct OPPM to establish annual performance goals and review processes for agencies that reflect the President’s agenda.

title: Keep and strengthen the Made in America Office
proposal: The chapter recommends continuing and strengthening OMB's Made in America Office, which oversees Buy-American commitments.
quote: Made-in-America commitments. Its work ought to be continued and further strengthened.

title: Keep White House review of rules, including Treasury tax rules
proposal: The President should keep Executive Order 12866, which sets White House (OIRA) review of regulations, and keep its recent extension to Treasury Department regulations.
quote: The Administration should likewise maintain the recent extension of those standards to regulatory actions of the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

title: Require White House review of 'independent' agency rules
proposal: Agencies that have historically been treated as independent should also have to do regulatory analysis and submit their rules for OIRA review.
quote: Regulatory analysis and OIRA review should also be required of the historically “independent” agencies as the Office of Legal Counsel has found is legally permissible.

title: Undo Biden changes to regulatory review and cost-benefit rules
proposal: If the Biden administration changes Executive Order 12866 or OMB Circular A-4 on cost-benefit analysis, the next President should undo those changes and aim for the least burdensome rules possible.
quote: develop a rigorous, data-driven approach that will result in the least burdensome rules possible.

title: Increase funding for OIRA
proposal: The chapter says funding for OMB's regulatory review office has shrunk over the years and recommends reversing that trend.
quote: Yet over the years, funding for OIRA has diminished. This trend should be reversed.

title: Create OIRA 'regulatory advance teams'
proposal: The budget should fund OIRA staff to form teams that advise agencies on cost-benefit analysis at the start of writing major rules, kept separate from the staff who later review those rules.
quote: employees to form regulatory advance teams that would consult with agencies on cost-benefit analysis and good regulatory practices at the beginning of the rulemaking process

title: Reinstate Trump-era regulatory executive orders
proposal: The next President should bring back several Trump regulatory executive orders, including EO 13771 and EO 13891 (which required OIRA review of significant guidance documents), with changes as needed.
quote: The next President should also reinstate the many executive orders signed by President Trump that were designed to make the regulatory process more just, efficient, and transparent.

title: Strengthen the federalism executive order
proposal: Executive Order 13132 on federalism should be strengthened so federal 'cooperative federalism' programs do not take over state regulatory and budget operations.
quote: on federalism should be strengthened so that state regulatory and fiscal operations are not commandeered by the federal

title: Issue an updated Reagan-era order on property takings
proposal: The President should revise and sign an updated version of Reagan's Executive Order 12630 on government actions that affect private property rights.
quote: Additionally, the President should revise and sign an updated version of President Ronald Reagan’s Executive Order

title: Enforce information-quality, paperwork and privacy laws more strongly
proposal: The President should strengthen use of the Information Quality Act, the Paperwork Reduction Act, and the Privacy Act, and make sure OIRA's statistics and information policy work is done well.
quote: and ensure the sound execution of OIRA’s statistical and other information policy functions.

title: Revise OMB's uniform grants guidance
proposal: OIRA should work with other parts of OMB to revise OMB's Guidance for Grants and Agreements and make sure grant and contract rules meet regulatory review standards.
quote: OIRA should also work with other components of OMB to revise and apply OMB’s uniform Guidance for Grants and Agreements

title: Pass regulatory reform laws such as the REINS Act
proposal: The President should work with Congress to pass regulatory reform laws, naming the Regulatory Accountability Act, SMART Act, GOOD Act, Early Participation in Regulations Act, Unfunded Mandates Accountability and Transparency Act, and REINS Act.
quote: But executive reforms and actions, while vital, are not enough: Congress also must act. The next President should work with Congress to pass significant

title: Pass the Midnight Rules Relief Act
proposal: Congress and the President should pass the Midnight Rules Relief Act so Congress can overturn several last-minute rules of a prior administration in a single vote under the Congressional Review Act.
quote: To leverage the CRA’s power to the maximum extent, Congress and the President should enact the Midnight Rules Relief Act

title: Use OMB legislative clearance to enforce message consistency
proposal: The OMB Director should actively use OMB's power to clear agency testimony and legislative views to keep the executive branch's policy and messages consistent.
quote: The Director should use these authorities to enforce policy and message consistency aggressively

title: Eliminate NSC directorates not aligned with the President
proposal: The National Security Advisor should review National Security Council directorates, eliminate those not aligned with the President's agenda, and create new ones for the President's priorities.
quote: the NSA should immediately evaluate and eliminate directorates that are not aligned with the President’s agenda and replace them with new directorates

title: Assign senior NSC officials to carry out specific initiatives
proposal: The National Security Advisor should make named senior NSC officials responsible for carrying out specific policy initiatives with measurable deadlines.
quote: the NSA should assign responsibility for implementation of specific policy initiatives to senior NSC officials from across the NSC staff structure.

title: Let the NSC handle its own security clearances
proposal: The NSC should have the resources and authority to grant and hold security clearances for its own staff, using investigators who work only for the NSC.
quote: and the NSC should be adequately resourced and authorized to adjudicate and hold security clearances internally with investigators who work directly for the NSC

title: White House review of defense strategy and war plans
proposal: The NSC and OMB should give priority to White House review of the National Defense Strategy and review war plans, force planning, and key defense, State, and intelligence guidance.
quote: the National Defense Strategy, which by tradition has evaded significant review, should be prioritized for White House review by the NSC and OMB.

title: NSC review of all general and flag officer promotions
proposal: The NSC should closely review all promotions of generals and admirals to put core military roles ahead of issues such as climate change and critical race theory.
quote: The NSC should rigorously review all general and flag officer promotions to prioritize the core roles and responsibilities of the military over social engineering and non-defense matters

title: Merge the Homeland Security Council and cyber office into the NSC
proposal: The NSC staff should take over the functions of the Homeland Security Council and bring in the Office of the National Cyber Director.
quote: The NSC staff will need to consolidate the functions of both the NSC and the Homeland Security Council (HSC), incorporate the recently established Office of the National Cyber Director
agency: NSC / HSC / Office of the National Cyber Director

title: Send nonessential NSC detailees home on day one
proposal: The National Security Advisor should return all nonessential staff on loan from other agencies on the first day and soon replace essential ones with staff aligned with the new President.
quote: detailees to their home agencies on their first day in office so that the new Administration can proceed efficiently

title: Give the NSC its own legal counsel
proposal: The NSC should have its own lawyer to advise on legal options for the President, with the White House Counsel also part of the process.
quote: For instance, the NSC needs its own counsel to inform what legal options can be provided to the President.

title: NEC head should chair regular EOP coordination meetings
proposal: The National Economic Council director should lead a standing meeting with the heads of other Executive Office of the President offices.
quote: and Office of Science and Technology Policy. To this end, the NEC Director should chair a standing meeting with the principals

title: Coordinate all international economic policy from the NEC
proposal: The White House should set clear council jurisdictions at the start, and international economic policy should be coordinated only by the National Economic Council, not jointly with the NSC.
quote: To avoid such problems, international economic policy should be entirely coordinated from NEC.

title: Empower USTR and drop legacy trade advisory committees
proposal: The U.S. Trade Representative should lead trade policy from the White House with enough budget and staff, use interagency trade committees, and get rid of old advisory committees whose members serve special interests.
quote: drive a consensus among federal stakeholders, dispose of legacy advisory committees with members who serve special interests, direct action to implement policy priorities

title: Give the Council of Economic Advisers a seat on all policy
proposal: The White House Chief of Staff should make sure the Council of Economic Advisers takes part in policymaking on all relevant issues as the White House's in-house economists.
quote: Structurally, the White House Chief of Staff should ensure that the CEA has a seat at the

title: Hire CEA economists on the White House calendar through PPO
proposal: The administration should consider hiring senior CEA economists starting in mid-January and through the Office of Presidential Personnel, instead of on an academic-year cycle.
quote: A future Administration should consider hiring that reflects the White House calendar (mid-January) and involves the Office of Presidential Personnel.

title: Raise the profile of the White House science office director
proposal: If science is being manipulated at agencies, the President should increase the formal or informal standing of the Office of Science and Technology Policy director.
quote: the President should increase the prominence of the OSTP’s Director either formally or informally.

title: Narrow the 'Industries of the Future' research priorities
proposal: The list of research priority areas called Industries of the Future should be reviewed and narrowed to match the next administration's priorities.
quote: and narrowed to ensure consistency with the next Administration’s priorities.

title: Reshape the U.S. Global Change Research Program by executive order
proposal: The President should issue an executive order to reshape the U.S. Global Change Research Program and related climate research, including requiring diverse viewpoints in its assessments.
quote: The President should also issue an executive order to reshape the U.S. Global Change Research Program (USGCRP)

title: Check the independence of climate research contractors
proposal: OSTP and OMB should jointly review how independent the outside contractors are who do much of the government research used for policymaking.
quote: The OSTP and OMB should jointly assess the independence of the contractors used to conduct much of this outsourced

title: Review and possibly reject Biden-era climate assessments
proposal: The next President should closely examine and, if needed, refuse to accept any Global Change Research Program assessment, such as the National Climate Assessment, prepared under the Biden administration.
quote: The next President should critically analyze and, if required, refuse to accept any USGCRP assessment prepared under the Biden Administration.

title: Limit White House climate research groups to advisory roles
proposal: The President should limit OSTP, the NSTC environment committee, climate research working groups, and similar EOP bodies to purely informational and advisory roles.
quote: The President should also restore related EOP research components to their purely informational and advisory roles.

title: Separate scientific risk assessment from risk management
proposal: The administration should keep the scientific job of assessing risks separate from decisions on managing risks, which the chapter says belong to elected officials and the public.
quote: the new Administration should separate the scientific risk assessment function from the risk management function

title: Remove gender, racial equity and climate initiatives from science policy
proposal: The administration should reverse Biden-era gender, racial equity, and climate initiatives in science policy and remove them from policy manuals and guidance, making scientific excellence OSTP's top priority.
quote: should be reversed and scrubbed from all policy manuals, guidance documents, and agendas, and scientific excellence and innovation should be restored as the OSTP’s top priority.

title: Rewrite NEPA rules and ban cumulative impact analysis
proposal: The President should have the Council on Environmental Quality rewrite its environmental review (NEPA) rules like the 2020 version, including banning cumulative impact analysis, and go further to speed reviews.
quote: rewrite its regulations implementing NEPA along the lines of the historic 2020 effort and restoring its key provisions such as banning the use of cumulative impact analysis.

title: Limit court review of NEPA environmental analyses
proposal: New NEPA rules should be written to narrow the scope of court review of agencies' environmental analyses and the remedies courts can order.
quote: It should frame the new regulations to limit the scope for judicial review of agency NEPA analysis and judicial remedies

title: Give the permitting council's director authority over agencies
proposal: The President should make the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council's executive director an Executive Office appointee with delegated authority to direct permitting agencies.
quote: further empower the FPISC by making its Executive Director an EOP appointee with delegated presidential directive authority over executive branch permitting agencies.
agency: Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council / CEQ

title: New executive order for one unified infrastructure permitting process
proposal: The President should issue an executive order creating a single process for approving major infrastructure projects that gives project sponsors more control over review timelines.
quote: The new President should seek to issue a new executive order to create a unified process for major infrastructure projects

title: Create a White House Senior Advisor for energy and environment
proposal: The President should issue an executive order creating a Senior Advisor, reporting to the Chief of Staff, to coordinate energy and environment policy across the Executive Office of the President.
quote: The President should issue an executive order establishing a Senior Advisor to coordinate the policy development and implementation of relevant energy and environment policy

title: Abolish the Office of Domestic Climate Policy
proposal: The same executive order should abolish the White House Office of Domestic Climate Policy.
quote: officials across the EOP (for example, the policy staff of the NSC, NEC, DPC, CEQ, and OSTP) and abolishing the existing Office of Domestic
agency: White House Office of Domestic Climate Policy

title: Eliminate the Social Cost of Carbon working group and its use
proposal: The President should eliminate the interagency working group on the Social Cost of Carbon and, by executive order, end the use of social cost of carbon analysis.
quote: The President should eliminate the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Carbon (SCC), which is cochaired by the OSTP

title: Overhaul the federal permitting system with Congress
proposal: The President should work with Congress on a broad modernization of permitting across all agencies to reduce lawsuit risk and let agencies issue programmatic, general, and provisional permits.
quote: Finally, the President should work with Congress to establish a sweeping

title: Drug policy director should consult border enforcement officials
proposal: With fentanyl deaths as the top drug priority, the director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy should consult with federal border enforcement officials.
quote: For these reasons, the Director of ONDCP should make it a point to consult with federal border enforcement officials.

title: Put a political appointee over the drug office's budget
proposal: A political appointee, not a career official, should lead the ONDCP budget office, and ONDCP should be run by political appointees committed to the administration's agenda.
quote: it is imperative that a political appointee lead the ONDCP budget office to ensure coordination between the OMB Program Associate Director and the ONDCP budgetary appointee.

title: Move ONDCP grant programs to DOJ and HHS
proposal: The chapter says the Drug-Free Communities and High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas grant programs should eventually be moved out of ONDCP to the Justice Department and HHS.
quote: While it makes sense to transfer these programs eventually to the Department of Justice and Department of Health and Human Services, respectively

title: Make sure drug grants fund the President's priorities
proposal: In the meantime, the ONDCP director should make sure its grants fund the President's drug control priorities rather than nonprofits the authors describe as having leftist agendas.
quote: it is vital that the ONDCP Director ensure in the immediate term that these grant programs are funding the President’s drug control priorities

title: Abolish the White House Gender Policy Council
proposal: The President should revoke Executive Order 14020 and every policy and guidance document tied to the Gender Policy Council, abolishing the council.
quote: every policy, including subregulatory guidance documents, produced on behalf of or related to the establishment or promotion of the Gender Policy Council and its subsidiary issues.

title: Create a White House lead for life and family issues
proposal: The President should appoint a Special Assistant to the President or higher to coordinate the administration's domestic policies on promoting life and family, working with the Domestic Policy Council.
quote: the President should appoint a position/point of contact with the rank of Special Assistant to the President or higher to coordinate and lead the

title: Include Vice President's staff in all policy processes
proposal: Office of the Vice President staff should be part of every policy process, including budget and regulatory review, from the first day of the administration.
quote: the OVP should have a seat at the table through every phase of policy development.
